title: Dense open orbit fibres from purely inseparable invariant function fields
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $a:W\to X$ an H-projective surjective morphism of integral finite-type $k$-schemes inducing a finite extension of function fields. Let a finite group $N$ act on $W$ by $k$-scheme automorphisms such that $a$ is invariant, and assume $k(W)^N/k(X)$ is purely inseparable. There is a dense nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$ such that $a^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}S\to U$ is finite surjective. The affine quotient $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}(S^N)$ is finite surjective with geometric fibres the $N$-orbits, and the induced finite morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(S^N)\to U$ is radicial and surjective. Moreover
$$\operatorname{Frac}(S^N)=\operatorname{Frac}(S)^N.$$
Consequently every geometric fibre of $a^{-1}U\to U$ is a nonempty single $N$-orbit. In positive characteristic $p$, the open can be chosen with an integer $m\geq0$ such that $t^{p^m}\in R$ for every $t\in S^N$; in characteristic zero it can be chosen with $S^N=R$. No normality, faithfulness or freeness of the action is assumed.

H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target [def-kun-projective]. The other notions use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-radicial-morphism], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-pc-field-tower]. The fixed ring $S^N$ consists of elements fixed by every group element; $\operatorname{Frac}$ denotes the fraction field of a domain.

proof.text: The finite-type hypothesis on $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives a finite cover of $X$ by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A_j$ with $A_j$ finitely generated $k$-algebras. These rings are Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] and these opens are quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so $X$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact, i.e. Noetherian in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-generic-finite-morphism-open-neighborhood]. The H-projective convention is exactly [def-kun-projective]; by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] and [def-weil-proper-morphism] the morphism $a$ is separated and of finite type, i.e. quasi-compact and locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and it is quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Since $W$ and $X$ are integral, hence irreducible, they have unique generic points $\xi$ and $\eta$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]; $\eta$ is the generic point of the only irreducible component of $X$. Moreover $a(\xi)=\eta$: the closure of $a(\xi)$ contains $a(\overline{\{\xi\}})=a(W)=X$ by continuity and surjectivity.

proof.text: We show $a^{-1}(\{\eta\})=\{\xi\}$. Let $w\in W$ with $a(w)=\eta$. Choose a nonempty affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$; it contains $\eta$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] $w$ lies in an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq a^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] $A$ and $B$ are domains, $\operatorname{Spec}A\ni\eta$, $\operatorname{Spec}B\ni\xi$, and the germ maps identify $\operatorname{Frac}A=k(X)$, $\operatorname{Frac}B=k(W)$; the residue fields at $\eta,\xi$ are these generic stalks, which are fields. The ring map $A\to B$ is compatible with the given finite extension $k(X)\to k(W)$, hence injective. The prime $\mathfrak p_w\subset B$ of $w$ contracts to the prime $(0)$ of $A$ corresponding to $\eta$. Put $\Sigma=A\setminus\{0\}$. The domain $\Sigma^{-1}B\subseteq k(W)$ is a $k(X)$-subspace of the finite-dimensional $k(X)$-space $k(W)$, so it is a field by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field]. Since $\mathfrak p_w\cap\Sigma=\emptyset$, $\Sigma^{-1}\mathfrak p_w$ is a proper ideal of this field, hence zero, and so $\mathfrak p_w=0$ because $B\subseteq\Sigma^{-1}B$. Thus $w$ is the generic point of the dense open $\operatorname{Spec}B$, i.e. $w=\xi$. The fibre of $a$ over the generic point $\eta$ of the only irreducible component of $X$ is therefore finite, and with Step 1 all hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-generic-finite-morphism-open-neighborhood] hold. It gives a dense open $V\subseteq X$ containing $\eta$ such that $a^{-1}V\to V$ is finite.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ containing the generic point of $X$ inside $V$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target] the restriction is still finite, hence $a^{-1}U_0=\operatorname{Spec}S_0$ with $S_0$ a finite $R_0$-module by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. It is surjective by restricting the given surjection. Both opens are nonempty and integral. The fraction-field theorem [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] identifies $\operatorname{Frac}(R_0)=k(X)$ and $\operatorname{Frac}(S_0)=k(W)$ through the germ maps, so the given field inclusion makes $R_0\to S_0$ injective. We regard these rings as subrings of $k(W)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $U_0$: $R_0$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra, so [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] makes it Noetherian directly. Invariance of $a$ makes its inverse image $N$-stable and makes $N$ fix $R_0$ pointwise.

proof.text: Put $T_0=S_0^N$. This is an $R_0$-submodule of $S_0$: the action fixes $R_0$ and is additive. Since $R_0$ is Noetherian and $S_0$ is a finite $R_0$-module, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] gives generators $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ of $T_0$ as an $R_0$-module. We can include $1$ among them. The single-affine-cover criterion in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target] now shows that $\operatorname{Spec}T_0\to U_0$ is finite: its entire affine target has affine inverse image with the displayed finite coordinate algebra.

source.place: Tag 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic), submodules of finite modules; morphisms.tex Tag 01WI (lemma-finite-local), single-affine-cover criterion.

proof.text: The affine-pairs criterion [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], applied to the original finite-type structure morphism $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the affine open $\operatorname{Spec}S_0$, says that $S_0$ is a finite-type $k$-algebra. Thus this affine scheme is locally of finite type over $k$. It is separated over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], and every $N$-orbit lies in this single affine open. Apply [lem-sfb-admissible-finite-type-field-quotient]: the quotient is $q_0:\operatorname{Spec}S_0\to\operatorname{Spec}T_0$, is finite and surjective, and its geometric fibres are precisely $N$-orbits. The inclusion $R_0\subseteq T_0$ gives $b_0:\operatorname{Spec}T_0\to U_0$, with $a|_{U_0}=b_0q_0$.

proof.text: Here is the fixed fraction-field calculation without normality. Certainly $\operatorname{Frac}(T_0)\subseteq\operatorname{Frac}(S_0)^N$. Conversely, write a fixed fraction as $x=u/v$ with $u,v\in S_0$ and $v\ne0$. Put $d=\prod_{h\in N}h(v)$. This is nonzero and fixed, and $xd=u\prod_{h\ne1}h(v)$ belongs to $S_0$. Since $x$ and $d$ are fixed in the fraction field, $xd$ belongs to $T_0$. Therefore $x=(xd)/d\in\operatorname{Frac}(T_0)$, proving equality. In particular every $t_i$ belongs to the assumed purely inseparable extension $k(W)^N/k(X)$.

source.place: Agent-written norm-denominator calculation for X Lemma 2.2(iii), printed pp.149--150; expands the generic invariant-field assertion with no normality assumption.

proof.text: Suppose first that $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. By [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], choose $n_i\ge0$ with $t_i^{p^{n_i}}\in\operatorname{Frac}(R_0)$. Set $m=\max_i n_i$ and $q=p^m$. Then $t_i^q\in\operatorname{Frac}(R_0)$ for every $i$; write $t_i^q=c_i/d_i$ with $c_i,d_i\in R_0$, $d_i\ne0$, and choose $f=\prod_i d_i\ne0$. If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, the same definition gives $k(W)^N=k(X)$, so write $t_i=c_i/d_i$ and choose the same product $f$. These are fractions in the embedded base field from Step 3, not elements of the normalization of $R_0$.

source.place: Tag 09HE (definition-purely-inseparable), including its arbitrary-characteristic convention; agent-written finite-generator denominator choice.

proof.text: Shrink to $U=D(f)\subseteq U_0$ and set $R=(R_0)_f$, $S=(S_0)_f$, $T=(T_0)_f$. The principal-localization open immersion [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] and the pullback formula [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-pullback] identify $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $a^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}S$. Since $f\ne0$ in the domain $R_0$, $U$ contains the generic point and is dense nonempty. Because $f$ is fixed and $S_0$ embeds in its fraction field, a fraction $s/f^j$ is fixed exactly when every $h(s)=s$; hence $S^N=T$. The $t_i$ still generate $T$ over $R$. In characteristic $p$, for $t=\sum_i a_it_i$ with $a_i\in R$, repeated binomial expansion gives $t^q=\sum_i a_i^q t_i^q\in R$ (the intermediate binomial coefficients for a $p$th power are divisible by $p$). In characteristic zero every $t_i\in R$, so $R\subseteq T\subseteq R$ and $T=R$. The fixed-field calculation of Step 6 applies to $S$ as well, giving $\operatorname{Frac}(S^N)=\operatorname{Frac}(S)^N$.

source.place: Tag 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine); modules.tex Tag 0H78 (remark-pullback-s-open). Agent-written invariant-fraction and Frobenius computations after the explicit denominator choice in Step 6.

proof.text: The finite morphisms $a|_{U_0}$, $q_0$, and $b_0$ restrict over $D(f)$ to finite morphisms $a|_U$, $q:\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}T$, and $b:\operatorname{Spec}T\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target]; the quotient restricts as asserted in [lem-sfb-admissible-finite-type-field-quotient]. The maps $a|_U$ and $q$ are surjective by restriction to these inverse images, so $b$ is surjective from $a|_U=bq$. To prove $b$ radicial, use the field-point criterion in [def-weil-radicial-morphism]. For two ring maps $\phi,\psi:T\to K$ to any field that agree on $R$, in characteristic $p$ one has $\phi(t)^q=\phi(t^q)=\psi(t^q)=\psi(t)^q$ for every $t$; hence $(\phi(t)-\psi(t))^q=0$ forces equality. In characteristic zero $T=R$. Thus $b$ is radicial in both cases.

proof.text: Fix $x\in U$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(x)$, with its canonical map $\alpha:R\to\Omega$. In characteristic $p$, for $t\in T$ define $\beta(t)$ as the unique root of $Z^q-\alpha(t^q)$ in $\Omega$: existence follows from [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and uniqueness from $(z-z')^q=0$. The identities $(t+u)^q=t^q+u^q$ and $(tu)^q=t^qu^q$ show by uniqueness that $\beta$ preserves addition, multiplication and $1$; also $\beta(r)=\alpha(r)$ for $r\in R$. Thus $\beta:T\to\Omega$ extends $\alpha$ and is unique by Step 9. In characteristic zero use $T=R$. Write $y=\ker\beta$. The injection $T/y\to\Omega$ extends to its fraction field $\kappa(y)$, and $\kappa(x)\subseteq\kappa(y)\subseteq\Omega$. Since $\Omega$ is algebraic over $\kappa(x)$, the same polynomial equations show that it is algebraic over $\kappa(y)$; it is therefore an algebraic closure of $\kappa(y)$ as well. The geometric-fibre assertion of [lem-sfb-admissible-finite-type-field-quotient] now applies exactly to $q$ over $y$ with this closure. Its geometric fibre has underlying point set nonempty and one $N$-orbit.

source.place: Agent-written geometric-point assembly of X Lemma 2.2(iii), printed pp.149--150; the quotient orbit assertion is Stacks groupoids.tex Tag 03BL (lemma-points). Root lifting uses the definition of algebraically closed field.

proof.text: Interpret Step 10 on geometric fibre schemes [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Both $a|_U$ and $q$ are finite, so their base changes along the displayed $\Omega$-points are finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]. Each fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a finite $\Omega$-algebra by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], hence integral over $\Omega$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. For every prime $P\subset A$, [lem-a1-integral-residue-extension-algebraic] makes $\kappa(P)/\Omega$ algebraic. It equals $\Omega$: a polynomial for any element factors into linear factors over the algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and a product vanishes in a field only when a factor vanishes. A point $P$ thus determines a unique $\Omega$-algebra map $A\to\Omega$, and conversely such a map determines its kernel. This correspondence respects $N$. For the fibre of $q$, Step 10 therefore gives a nonempty single orbit of $\Omega$-points. Every $\Omega$-point of $a|_U$ above $\alpha$ maps to the unique extension $\beta$ by Step 9; conversely every point above $\beta$ maps to $\alpha$. These two sets of $\Omega$-points coincide equivariantly. Applying the same point correspondence to the fibre of $a|_U$ gives the required nonempty single $N$-orbit on its underlying point set. No reducedness of either fibre, normality, or faithfulness is asserted or used.
